To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the thermodynamic parameters of 25 sequence symmetric and asymmetric tandem mismatches, which were previously unmeasured, have been determined and the parameters of the previous predictive model have been updated.
the thermodynamic parameters of 25 sequence asymmetric tandem mismaches were experimentally characterized and the predictive model for sequence asymmetric tandem mismathces was improved.

25 frequently occurring RNA tandem mismatches were characterized experimentally and a model for predicting the thermodynamic parameters of tandem mismatches was updated using these new experimental values.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermodynamics of RNA duplex formation.
thermodynamic characterization of tandem mismatch structures.
the thermodynamics of RNA duplexes that contain tandem mismatches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work has provided a thermodynamic characterization of the 25 most frequent tandem mismatches found within the 3,500,000 RNA sequences in the Rfam 9.0 database, and that these data have been combined with data from the literature to provide a more accurate predictive model.
the model proposed here is an improved version of the previous model.
the new experimental data and the updated predictive model provide the best available information for predicting the free energy of tandem mismatches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermodynamics of sequence symmetric and sequence asymmetric tandem mismaches can be predicted to a high level of accuracy.

the new model is more accurate for predicting the thermodynamic parameters of tandem mismatches than the previous model, and that the new model predicts the thermodynamic parameters more accurately than a model that does not consider the effect of the flanking base pair.
we have experimentally characterized 25 frequently occurring sequence symmetric and sequence asymmetric tandem mismaches and updated a predictive model for sequence asymmetric tandem mismathces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tandem mismatches are more stable than previously believed, and this stability is sequence specific.

, for tandem mismatches, the thermodynamics of sequence symmetric tandem mismaches is very different than that of sequence asymmetric tandem mismaches, and that a predictive model that treats these two types of tandem mismatches differently is needed.

, although the previous model was able to predict the stability for most tandem mismatches reasonably well, it is still important to measure the thermodynamics of frequently occurring tandem mismaches.
